newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Two million Nigerians have AIDS virus - minister.
newsitem.headline: Two million Nigerians have AIDS virus - minister.

text.p: Health Minister Ihechukwu Madubuike said in remarks reported in newspapers on Thursday that about two million people were infected with the AIDS virus in Nigeria, Africa's most populous nation with 100 million people.

Maduduike told a news conference in the capital Abuja on Wednesday that the government was planning ways to help AIDS patients and also advised them to form themselves into groups that would attract support from government and corporate bodies.

"Part of the policy includes establishing more community based core projects across the country, where people living with AIDS will be involved in income-generating activities to reduce their dependency on others," he said.
The health authorities have long said that AIDS (Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome) was on the rise in Nigeria where promiscuity is prevalent.
AIDS destroys the body's natural immunity and leaves infected people helpless against other diseases.

AIDS was not identified in Nigeria until 1986 and in 1991 the country launched a campaign to control its spread. Each of Nigeria's 36 states and the federal capital territory Abuja has a coordinator for the AIDS campaign.
